artworks.title: Orpheus
artworks.description: Moreau's symbolist Orpheus — lyre, laurel, and the Pierian melancholy Ovid and Apollodorus fixed in the tradition.

artworks.title: Orpheus Leading Eurydice from the Underworld
artworks.description: Corot's silvery twilight catches the pair mid-passage: Orpheus lifts his lyre like a lantern while Eurydice follows a half-step behind, the fatal backward glance only moments away. Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

artworks.title: Orpheus and Eurydice
artworks.description: Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada and now in the Museo del Prado, Rubens stages the underworld bargain: Orpheus leads Eurydice past Hades and Persephone as the fatal glance still hangs unmade. Eurydice is the luminous prize of the ascent — the bride the lyre almost brings home.

artworks.title: Landscape with Orpheus and Eurydice
artworks.description: Poussin sets the Thracian singer in a classical landscape at the moment of Eurydice's death by snakebite — marriage crowns cast aside, smoke rising beyond the trees. The Louvre canvas makes Orpheus' music a calm centre against catastrophe.

music.title: L'Orfeo
music.description: Monteverdi's Mantua favola in musica — Orpheus' descent and the fatal glance that opera never stopped restaging.

music.title: Orfeo ed Euridice
music.description: Gluck's reform opera — the underworld bargain stripped to voice and dance, Eurydice lost and (in the Vienna ending) restored.

films.title: Black Orpheus
films.description: Camus' Rio Carnival retelling — Orpheus and Eurydice among the favelas, Palme d'Or myth in samba time.
